extra.message: The NS_SCAN_GEOMETRY cookie value is concatenated directly into a shell command that is executed via new ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", command).start(). An authenticated user who can upload a document can inject arbitrary shell metacharacters (e.g. '; curl ...') through the cookie and achieve remote command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: handoff() parses a partner JWT with JWTParser.parse() and immediately trusts getSubject() to look up the user, without ever verifying the JWT signature, issuer, or audience. Because the channel /handoff route is public, an attacker can forge an unsigned/self-signed JWT with any subject (e.g. an admin email) to obtain a valid session token for that account.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The CSV field c[2] (business name) is concatenated into a native SQL query: "select count(*) from borrower_lead where business_name = '" + c[2].trim() + "'". Although the endpoint requires admin, a crafted business name such as "x' OR '1'='1" or "x'; DROP TABLE ...;--" modifies the query, allowing SQL injection against the database.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The stored product.rateExpression is evaluated with ognl.Ognl.getValue(). OGNL expressions can invoke arbitrary methods and static classes, so a rate expression supplied to the admin product endpoint (or seeded directly in the database) is evaluated as code and can achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: A Jackson ObjectMapper is configured with activateDefaultTyping(LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator.instance, NON_FINAL) and used to readValue() on the attacker-supplied formatSpec field. Laissez-faire default typing enables polymorphic deserialization gadget chains and is a well-known remote code execution vector.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() is used with default settings to parse a user-uploaded XML feed (importTransactions). External entities and DTDs are not disabled, so an attacker can submit XML containing a DOCTYPE/external entity to read local files or perform SSRF (XXE).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The NS_STMT_FILTER cookie is concatenated into an XPath expression: "//balance[account='" + filter + "']", which is compiled and evaluated. A value such as "'] | //* | //x['" injects arbitrary XPath and can alter the query result (XPath injection).

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: The user-supplied principal is concatenated into an LDAP search filter: "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + principal + "))". An admin can inject filter syntax (e.g. "*)(|(uid=*" or "*)(objectClass=*") to broaden the search or enumerate directory entries (LDAP injection).

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: The X-Core-Region request header is used verbatim as the base URL for an outbound HTTP request: URI.create(base + "/core/business/" + reference). An underwriter or admin can point the server at arbitrary internal or external hosts, enabling SSRF.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: testWebhook() uses the attacker-supplied X-Callback-Override header directly as the destination URL for an outbound request, bypassing the endpoint allowlist enforced when the webhook was created. This allows server-side request forgery to arbitrary URLs.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: brandingLogo() resolves the uploaded file name against the branding directory without normalization or a prefix check: brandStore.resolve(logo.fileName()). A multipart filename containing ../ sequences (or an absolute path) lets an admin overwrite arbitrary files on the server via Files.write(..., TRUNCATE_EXISTING).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The transition handler redirects to the user-controlled returnTo form parameter (Response.seeOther(URI.create(returnTo))) without validating that it is a local path, allowing an open redirect to an arbitrary external site (often chained with phishing/token theft).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The application purpose is rendered with {view.model.purpose.raw}, which disables Qute HTML escaping. A borrower controls the purpose field (create/edit application), so malicious HTML/JavaScript is stored and executed for any underwriter/admin viewing the credit file (stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The summary() endpoint builds an HTML response by string concatenation and inserts the user-supplied caption query parameter (and application fields) without HTML encoding. Reflecting markup such as <script>...</script> in the page enables reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: NoticeRenderer.render() passes a caller-supplied template string to Velocity.evaluate(). In WebResource.notice() the template is taken from the NS_NOTICE_TEMPLATE cookie, giving any authenticated user control of the Velocity template source. Velocity permits arbitrary object/method access, so this is server-side template injection leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: provisionConsole() and accessConsole() (lines 1323-1324) store and verify console passwords using unsalted MD5 (DigestUtils.md5Hex). MD5 is fast and collision-prone and is unsuitable for password storage, making hashes trivially crackable.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: A fixed admin account (auditor@northstar.local) is provisioned at startup with a hardcoded password ("Northstar#Audit2026") baked into the source. Anyone with the source/binaries can authenticate as a full admin.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: userDetail() returns the stored password hash to the admin in a field named credentialRecord (out.put("credentialRecord", u.passwordHash)). Exposing password hashes over the API increases the impact of any data leak and is unnecessary for support workflows.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: In upload(), if the caller is a support_specialist and supplies any non-blank X-Support-Branch header, the ownership check access.document(actor, id) is skipped and the document is loaded by raw id (LoanDocument.findById(id)). Any support_specialist can therefore upload/replace documents on arbitrary applications, bypassing per-application authorization (IDOR/broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PartnerEmbedFilter reflects the request Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, for all dashboard/application/document paths. Any malicious origin can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The X-Frame-Options header is removed for any HTML response whenever the request carries an NS_PARTNER_VIEW cookie, so an attacker can suppress clickjacking protection by setting that cookie and frame sensitive pages (e.g. dashboard, applications) in a hostile site.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: The DSESSION session cookie is created with .secure(false), and when an X-Legacy-Client header is present the SameSite policy is downgraded to NONE. This lets the session cookie be transmitted over plaintext HTTP and sent on cross-site requests, exposing it to interception and CSRF-style abuse.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: revenueReport() places the secret core signing key (key) directly in the URL query string (?apiKey=...). Query strings are commonly written to proxy/access logs and can leak the HMAC signing key, allowing forged core scope tokens.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: The public register/availability endpoint returns a distinct message ("This email is already registered.") when the X-App-Channel header equals "legacy", letting an unauthenticated attacker enumerate which email addresses have accounts.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: noteFailure() writes the raw submitted email address into a log line without sanitizing newline/control characters. An attacker can embed line breaks or forged log prefixes (e.g. "victim@x\nINFO admin login") to forge or corrupt audit/onboarding log entries (log injection).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: Statements and referral envelopes are decrypted with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding using a caller-supplied IV and no authentication tag (EnvelopeCodec follows the same pattern). The referral endpoint returns distinguishable responses for BadPaddingException versus other errors, so ciphertexts can be manipulated and probed, enabling a CBC padding oracle and undetected tampering.

cwe: CWE-353: Missing Support for Integrity Check
